Negotiators from Australia and China met for a third day in Geneva, according to two people familiar with the talks who were not authorised to speak publicly.

Customs data published last month showed exports to China falling for a third consecutive quarter, and industry groups in Canberra have pressed the government for a resolution before the end of the year.

A spokesperson for the trade department declined to comment on the substance of the talks. Analysts at the Lowy Institute said any agreement would likely be narrow. Beijing has not commented.
